proposals.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (~5 eV), electronically insulating oxide with good Li-ion conductivity. Its phosphate anion is oxidatively stable near 4 V vs Li, so it should block electron transfer between LiCoO2 and the chloride electrolyte. It is also a standard protective coating family for cathodes, and it is expected to be chemically compatible with Li3InCl6.
